long_biography.plain_text:
Valeriy Khoroshkovskyi moved repeatedly between corporate management and senior public administration. Trained as a lawyer in Kyiv, he entered business through metals trading, then developed interests across banking, consumer goods and manufacturing. Appointment as chief executive of Evraz gave him responsibility for a large international steel producer during a period of rapid expansion.

Khoroshkovskyi's government career included service as economy minister, customs chief, head of the Security Service, finance minister and first deputy prime minister. He left the Evraz role when returning to Ukrainian public office, illustrating the alternation between the two spheres. His cabinet service ended in 2012, after which his profile centred again on private investment.
